chapter_title: Concerning the Five Saviours, the Resurrectors of

fills.fill: wherein they have been laid low
fills.notes: ¶2 is concluding a statement about lives/powers being in something and needing a rising; the substrate idiom is spatial and impersonal (“laid low” in mixture/bondage), not moralizing. This sets up the list of “resurrectors” as successive modes/agents of re-ordering.

In the cosmological sequence the “second” after the primal initiator is the Living Spirit, whose function is to raise out what has fallen by constructing ordered supports (world-structure) and beginning separations. Fits the register: a named hypostasis, not a clerical title.
The Father is repeatedly defined in this layer as the “First established one” (the fixed, self-subsistent root of order). The phrase is resumed in ¶6, so restoring it here tightens the parallelism.
By his word all lives “shall be gathered” (performative word/order). A simple verbal support is required before “gather in and go to him.”
What is received at the Father in this substrate is not ‘forgiveness’ but reinvestiture: the lives regain their proper Light-form/garment and thus “rest” in their own degree.

fills.fill: he awakens the remembrance within them and turns their thought upward
fills.notes: Light Mind’s resurrecting work is interior: reorientation of mind/gnosis, the stirring of remembrance that loosens the binding forms. This keeps the impersonal correspondential logic (mind → awakening/turning) without later devotional coloring.
The phrase “to the good …” expects the class being raised; throughout this unit it is “lives” (living powers) rather than ‘souls’ in a later ecclesial sense.
Reasserts the Father’s defining property in this layer: stability/establishment as the ground for re-gathering.
The next clause is “all the powers,” so the governing verb must be a συλλογίζεσθαι-type action: gathering/collecting into order.
The Father ‘stands firm’ not in a place of mixture but at the fixed limit/term of the Light-realm; “boundary” is the correspondential term for the outermost of a kingdom where separation is effected.

What is ‘unveiled’ over powers in this cosmology is the seal/sign of their own region (mark of belonging and protection), not a sermon or decree. The seal is a boundary-action in correspondential terms.
Unveiling the seal has the effect of recognition—each power perceives its proper form and degree, enabling ascent/collection.
The drawing is explicitly extraction: the powers are pulled out of the mixed region (Darkness/compound) into their proper side.
“his will …” needs a verb of operation/impressing: the Father’s will acts as formative force, not as command; this is substrate-cosmological causality.
Parallels “resurrector”: to resurrect is literally to ‘stand up’ what was fallen; the text then continues “and he stands them up … there,” reinforcing the same root action.
The ‘there’ is not a generic heaven but each power’s proper station (correspondential: place = state/degree).
The terminal condition for remaining is not personal judgment but the completion of the cosmic separation/ordering—classic Iranian-Manichaean substrate telos.

assessment: Most gaps can be restored by the internal correspondential sequence: successive resurrectors (hypostases) act by (1) structural extraction/separation and (2) interior awakening/recognition, culminating in reintegration at the Father as the First Established. The tightest constraints were the recurring epithet “First established one” and the required verbs around “all the powers.” Several place/term phrases (boundary, mixture, separation) remain slightly underdetermined in exact wording, but the substrate register and cosmological logic constrain the sense strongly.
